headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP-enabled ECC can collide with spring-integration-samples via shared outputs, but direct pairwise interaction is undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and run browsers, so if spring-integration-samples content is copied into ECC workflows, malicious or malformed content could steer tool use. B itself shows no input-parsing surface, so the pathway is inferred from A’s permissive surfaces rather than directly documented interaction.
conditions: IF content from spring-integration-samples is pasted or synced into ECC-managed files or MCP inputs
IF ECC treats repository text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted repo text into ECC sessions
Use a separate workspace for spring-integration-samples
Review MCP inputs before execution
Turn off browser/tool actions for untrusted prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, git history, and files under ~/.claude, while spring-integration-samples is open-source and network-egress none. No shared workspace or sensitive data flow is documented, so leakage is only plausible if the operator places secrets into ECC and then exports them into B’s repo context.
conditions: IF sensitive material is stored in ECC session files or git history
IF that material is manually copied into spring-integration-samples artifacts
mitigations: Keep secrets out of ECC-managed files
Use separate directories for each agent
Clear session summaries before sharing outputs
Restrict repo contents to non-sensitive examples
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and network_egress allowlisted; B has no write capability documented, so direct conflict is asymmetric. Uncertainty about B’s runtime surfaces means the safest choice is medium rather than low, because ECC can still contend with shared files or git state if B is run in the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working tree
IF B is wrapped in a runtime that also mutates files or git state
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory
Avoid concurrent git operations
Snapshot the workspace before agent runs
Serialize file-writing tasks
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and persist session summaries, skills, and security findings, which B could consume as authoritative if the operator wires outputs together. B’s docs do not show verification or action-taking, so the cascade is inferred, but the pair still presents a default risk if ECC output is reused without review.
conditions: IF ECC outputs are fed into spring-integration-samples documentation or automation steps
IF B consumes ECC-produced text without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of ECC outputs before reuse
Mark generated text as untrusted
Separate analysis and execution steps
Keep B read-only when ingesting ECC output
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention, hooks, and security findings, while spring-integration-samples shows no regulated-data handling or residency constraints. No direct compliance mismatch is documented, so only a low-risk policy gap exists if operators place regulated data into ECC and then move it into B artifacts.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ECC session artifacts
IF that data is copied into spring-integration-samples outputs or logs
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in ECC sessions
Purge retention-sensitive files regularly
Use synthetic data for examples
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
